title: The carrier Junyō, 9 December 1944
eyebrow: South-west of Nagasaki · SEA DEVIL's and REDFISH's second war patrols

participants.name: Junyō
participants.note: returning from Mako to the home islands (the Navy summary); SEA DEVIL's radar had one very large pip, two large and four small, the task force never sighted; REDFISH took her for a SHOKAKU or HAYATAKA type carrier

paras.text: Two boats on one carrier in the night of 8–9 December 1944: SEA DEVIL's four stern torpedoes at 0028 I and REDFISH's attacks at 0156 and 0320 I, as typed on their attack sheets, beside the Navy's summary, which has Junyō torpedoed once, two hits, at 0130.

Junyō, returning from Mako, was torpedoed about 50 miles south-west of Nomozaki: two hits, but she could make 13 knots on one shaft and entered Sasebo about 1000 (p. 5) [[cite:jacar:C16120660300]]. The summary has one time, 0130 I, and does not say whose torpedoes. SEA DEVIL's narrative times two explosions at 0031:40 and 0031:55 I, each checking with a torpedo's run, and PLAICE signalled that she saw the hits: two hits, as the summary has, an hour before its time. REDFISH claimed one hit at 0156 I, 26 minutes after it, about 4 nm from the summary's place against SEA DEVIL's 17 nm, and one more at 0320 I nearer Nomozaki. Both boats' attacks are paired with the summary as probable or possible; which made the hits is open until a record with Junyō's own times is found.
Positions are each boat's own; lines between them are straight. Junyō is drawn from the boats' sightings, and no Japanese position is given in figures.
SEA DEVIL's sheets type zone I; REDFISH's Attack 7 sheet types a J that her positions file reads as I (her japanese.yml and claims.yml say why). Japanese records use Tokyo time (I, −9).

Junyō's own record and her escorts' December diaries: none found on JACAR by her name or the 21st Destroyer Division's. SEA POACHER, PLAICE and PIRANHA were in the area that night (SEA DEVIL's ship contacts) and are not in the kit.

War patrol reports, NARA microfilm M1752: SEA DEVIL Patrol 2 (74843922), REDFISH Patrol 2 (74837267). The Navy's day-by-day summary of escort and anti-submarine events, December 1944, via JACAR (C16120660300, National Institute for Defense Studies). Coastline: Natural Earth.

outcome.note: Junyō torpedoed, two hits. SEA DEVIL's two explosions (0031:40 and 0031:55 I) each checked with a torpedo's run, and PLAICE signalled that she saw the hits; REDFISH's Attack 7 (0156 I) claimed one hit. The summary's two hits fit SEA DEVIL's count and its place (about 50 miles south-west of Nomozaki) fits REDFISH's position better (about 4 nm, against 17 nm); its time (0130 I) falls between the two. Probable, not hit, until a record with Junyō's own times is found (her escorts' or Sasebo's December diaries)

words.type_attack: Night radar submerged approach. Dropped to periscope depth to let escorts by and tracked target by sound bearings from JP-2 and JK equipment. Fired by T.D.C. and spread by offset handle with radar bearings and ranges.
words.description: Contact was made by radar at range of 33,000 yards. The radar screen showed one very large pip, two large pips and four small pips at 28,000 yards. The night was overcast with poor visibility resulting in the task force never being sighted.
words.damaged: One large warship. Probably BB or CV.
words.determined_by: Two explosions timed exactly with the generated torpedo run to be torpedo hits in the target. A third explosion was heard that did not check with torpedo run to this target. Received a message from U.S.S. PLAICE saying they saw our hits.
words.target_line: Target Draft: 28 feet Course: 050°T Speed: 19 knots Range: 4315 yds.
words.own_ship: Speed: 4 knots Course: 161°T Depth: 42 feet Angle: 3° down
words.note: Tube 10 typed "Miss (?)". The narrative (p10-p11) times the attack to the second: 0005 dived to radar depth; 0027 commenced firing four Mk 23s from the stern tubes, range 4300 yards, 115° starboard track, depth set 6 feet, gyros 180°, "Although the torpedo runs were around 5000 yards, this was our only shot"; fired #7 0027:45, #8 0028:00, #9 0028:18, #10 0028:28; explosions 0031:40 ("checked exactly with #8 torpedo") and 0031:55 (#9); 0033:05 one explosion, unknown; 0035 pinging and screws close aboard, went deep; 0050 screws faded out. The sheet's intervals (10 sec.) round the narrative's 15, 18 and 10 seconds

words.description: Task Force consisting of one SHOKAKU or HAYATAKA type aircraft carrier, one battleship, three escorting destroyers. The aircraft carrier was attacked. Initial contact was by SJ Radar range 31,000 yards. Visibility at time of attack about 6,000 yds.
words.damaged: (EC) Damaged one SHOKAKU or HAYATAKA type aircraft carrier (29,800 tons).
words.determined_by: Commanding Officer on bridge observed one timed hit (2min. 10 sec) after commenced firing.
words.remarks: * At least one of these torpedoes ran erratic as determined by sound bearings after firing. It is not known which one. Unable to explain other misses. Course 050T. and speed 13 were used in estimate of course and speed. Plotting of definitely observed timed hit shows course 070T. speed 11. It is believed target was employing a modified constant helm zig plan.
words.note: The sheet types the time 0156 (J); positions.csv has zone I (the patrol's zone that week; Attack 8, 84 minutes later, is typed (I)). Kept as typed. The target course on the sheet (070, first digit faint) is the plotted one from the remarks, not the 050 set on the T.D.C. at firing. Tracks are typed without a side: with 070 they compute starboard and within 3 degrees of those typed (125S, 130S, 131S, 127S for tubes 3-6 against 124 30, 128, 128 30, 124), not checked by the tool, which needs a side. Erratic is typed * for tubes 2-6 (the remarks' asterisk).

words.type_attack: Night radar surface attack. Target zigged away during firing - T.D.C. was corrected and firing continued.
words.description: Task force as described in Attack No. 1. Visibility at this firing 12,000 yards.
words.damaged: (EC) Damaged one SHOKAKU or HAYATAKA type aircraft carrier (29,800 tons).
words.determined_by: One timed hit at 3min. 59 sec. after commenced firing.
words.remarks: * One premature explosion was observed at 2min. 15sec. after firing. It is not known which torpedo was the premature. Explosion observed by C.O. Target was seen to zig away during firing of torpedoes resulting in a greater track angle than at instant of commence firing. Course and speed of target estimated to be 050T. - 12.
words.note: "Task force as described in Attack No. 1" means this patrol's Attack 7 (the carrier group). Tracks are typed without a side. The sheet's one target course (035) gives about 156 starboard for tubes 1-3 and 160 and 155 for 4-6; the typed tracks of tubes 1 and 2 (140, 139) fit the course before the zig (about 050, the remarks' estimate), those of tubes 3-6 (154, 158, 158, 153) the corrected T.D.C. Kept as typed. The narrative times the first torpedo 0320.37 (positions.csv). Erratic * on tubes 1-5 marks the unidentified premature; tube 6 is the one typed Hit.
